- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (sentiment < 0.4) — add 3–7% to forecast to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model tends to overreact to recent price spikes — apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid immediate overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid sharp upward trends unless sentiment is consistently bullish (>0.6 over 5+ days) — cap upward momentum at +5% above prior 14-day high.
- If sentiment is volatile or oscillating (±0.25 range), reduce forecast smoothness — use 3-period moving average to dampen noise.
